title: AIC and BIC are not tests
dek: AIC estimates a predictive KL risk. BIC is a large-n approximation to a Bayes factor under a particular prior. Neither is a p-value, and neither requires nested models.
story: AIC = −2ℓ(θ̂) + 2p. Smaller is better as an estimate of expected out-of-sample Kullback–Leibler risk (up to a constant). The 2p penalty is not a significance threshold. A difference of 0.4 is a shrug, not a star.

BIC = −2ℓ(θ̂) + p log n. The heavier penalty is a crude Laplace approximation to a marginal likelihood. BIC tends to pick simpler models as n grows if a true finite-dimensional model is in the list. AIC does not; it keeps extra parameters that still predict.

You may compute AIC for non-nested mean structures. You may not treat ΔAIC as χ² or as a posterior probability without extra work (Akaike weights are a heuristic). If you needed a test of a restriction, you wanted an LRT — previous plates.
deepTitle: What n, what p, what likelihood
deep: n in BIC is the number of independent sampling units. Using n = SNPs or n = reads when isolates are the units is how BIC becomes a fiction. For mixed models, p is effective degrees of freedom, not a head-count of every uⱼ.

AIC needs a genuine log-likelihood. Quasi-likelihood, sandwich estimating equations, and composite likelihoods need modified criteria (if any). Cross-validation is often the more honest predictive score in a genomics pipeline.

Nested special case: LRT uses 2Δℓ vs χ²_k. AIC prefers the larger model when 2Δℓ > 2k, i.e. when the LRT statistic exceeds twice the extra parameters — a different threshold than χ²_{k, 0.95}. They answer different questions even when both are legal.
WAIC/LOO in Bayes and AIC in ML are cousins: prediction, not confirmation. Bayes factors (next Bayesian plates) are confirmation-like and prior-sensitive. Do not mix all four in one table caption.

example.title: Lineage term: test versus AIC
example.setup: Bernoulli GLM for FQ-R. Reduced: mutation only, p = 2, ℓ = −98.4. Full: + lineage, p = 3, ℓ = −97.1. n = 240 isolates.

steps.title: LRT
steps.body: Λ = 2(1.3) = 2.6 vs χ²_1. p ≈ 0.11. Do not reject at 5%.

steps.title: AIC
steps.body: ΔAIC = (−2ℓ_full + 2×3) − (−2ℓ_red + 2×2) = −2.6 + 2 = −0.6. Full slightly smaller AIC — a predictive shrug, not a discovery.

steps.title: BIC
steps.body: p log n ≈ log 240 ≈ 5.48 extra penalty. BIC prefers the reduced model decisively. Same two fits, three captions. Write which question you asked.

example.takeaway: Δℓ is one number. LRT, AIC, and BIC hang different signs on it. Pick the sign that matches the scientific job.

choices: A penalised log-likelihood estimate of relative predictive KL risk

check.why: That is Akaike’s target. Nestedness is not required. P-values are a different contract.

whyWrong.A Bayes factor: Closer to BIC’s motivation, and still not AIC.

check.prompt: On the small-multiples plate, why is the BIC “keep small” bar taller at n=100 than AIC’s?
check.figureHint: AIC panel threshold 2 vs BIC panel ~4.6.
choices: Because BIC always prefers the larger model
Because BIC’s penalty p log n is larger than AIC’s 2p for this n, so you need a bigger ℓ gain to prefer the extra parameter
Because LRT and BIC are the same at n=100
Because AIC is a posterior probability
